- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in the immediate follow-up period.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to the forecast shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.0) or mixed; model often overreacts; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- In 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.0” (neutral) with no clear trend, model tends to drift toward recent low; correct by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.
